transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-11 10:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marta Velasquez (Bluewave PM), Ethan Cho (Bluewave Platform Eng), Dana Liu (Bluewave Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen may be fuzzy): staging infra mostly provisioned; missing SSO test accounts and KMS mapping; need extra kv-cache bench; next week follow-up.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Jordan: okay, good morning everyone, thanks for hopping on. can you hear me alright?
[00:04] Marta: yes, hear you, thanks Jordan.
[00:07] Jordan: cool. quick agenda — two blockers we want to clear: access (SSO/RBAC/test users) and env readiness (VPC peering, egress, KMS). Priya will share bench results and tuning notes. then wrap with next steps. sound good?
[00:22] Ethan: yep that works, we have about an hour.
[00:25] Priya: good morning all — I'll start with a short readout on the perf runs we did last night, then go into kv-cache toggles. note: transcription may pick up some names wrong — sorry in advance.
[00:36] Priya: so baseline — we ran 3 steady-state passes hitting our staging endpoint with synthetic traffic at 400 rps, sequence length median 80 tokens, occasional 1k sequences. p95 latency without KV cache was about 420ms across our model variant (redwood-relic-3b-quant). with KV-cache enabled and prefix cache warm, p95 dropped to 210-260ms depending on the sequence mix.
[01:05] Marta: that's promising — what's the token cost delta when using cache?
[01:09] Priya: roughly 25-30% tokens saved on average for our conversational prompts. there is some variability — long multi-turn sessions save more.
[01:18] Ethan: are you using continuous batching? i think our staging traffic might need different batching profiles.
[01:22] Priya: yes, Redwood runtime did continuous batching; we set conservative max batch of 48 for the run. we can tune it down to lower p95 at the cost of throughput if that's your priority.
[01:31] Jordan: couple of notes — the benchmark spreadsheets are in the share drive link I sent, look under /benchmarks/bluewave. Priya, can you attach the raw CSVs?
[01:40] Priya: yeah will upload after call.
[01:42] Dana: quick security question on the cache — where is the cached KV stored? is it in customer VPC or in Redwood-managed memstore?
[01:50] Priya: right now for hosted POC we used Redwood-managed cache pinned to the customer's region. for Private deployments we support deploying cache within customer VPC but that needs the private runtime. for Dedicated there are options to pin to instance-local mem.
[02:05] Dana: okay we need to confirm data residency for the cached prefix — can't have persistent keys leaving our control.
[02:11] Jordan: noted. action: we'll document cache residency options and the steps to enable VPC-local cache.
[02:16] Marta: on access — Ethan tried SSO but we don't yet have test accounts provisioned to exercise RBAC. we need developer and ops roles to validate consoles and API keys.
[02:26] Ethan: yes, we created a service account but it's blocked by SAML assertion errors.
[02:31] Jordan: did you follow the SSO checklist? I sent a short SAML troubleshooting note earlier.
[02:36] Ethan: we followed but looks like the audience URI and cert fingerprint didn't match.
[02:40] Jordan: okay we'll re-send a tightened checklist and a sample metadata XML that should match your IdP. I'll put that in the readiness doc.
[02:48] Marta: ETA on that?
[02:50] Jordan: I'll share today, that's Jordan action item.
[02:53] Priya: also for RBAC, we'll need at least two test users: one with admin-esque console privileges and one with limited token-only access to simulate your app tier.
[03:04] Dana: and can you document what audit fields are emitted? we need object-level audit logs for compliance.
[03:09] Priya: yes, Redwood emits request id, model id, route, token counts, timestamp, and an anonymized user id when enabled. we'll share the audit schema. note: full prompt content retention is opt-in and can be disabled.
[03:23] Dana: okay that's important. we'll review the schema.
[03:27] Jordan: switching to env readiness: Ethan, where are we on VPC peering and test egress rules?
[03:34] Ethan: we've got the peering request open — waiting for the cloud networking team to accept. we also need help listing the egress FQDNs for your dedicated runtime so we can lock down outbound.
[03:44] Jordan: we have a published egress list in the ops doc, it's small rather than a massive CIDR range. I'll paste it into the chat after.
[03:51] Ethan: great, that will help. also, do we need to open any other ports for telemetry forwarding?
[03:56] Priya: typically we use TLS to an ingestion endpoint on 443; we can also use VPC endpoints for direct ingestion if you prefer.
[04:05] Marta: about KMS — Dana, can you summarize what we need?
[04:09] Dana: main ask is bring-your-own-key for secrets and rotations aligned to our policy. we also need a KMS integration that supports key aliasing and HSM-backed keys.
[04:20] Jordan: Redwood supports KMS integration for Private deployments and Dedicated via customer-managed keys. for hosted POC we can provision a scoped key but we understand you want BYOK for production.
[04:32] Dana: okay we'll capture that for the runbook.
[04:35] Priya: back to perf — we also tried a smaller model fallback for cold starts. when the main cluster is saturated, the router can redirect to a lower-cost variant; p95 there was about 650ms but should keep your SLA when combined with circuit-breaker policies.
[04:49] Ethan: do we get automatic fallback or is that manual config?
[04:52] Priya: policy-driven; you can set thresholds by latency, error rate, or queue depth. we can demo that control plane in a short follow-up if helpful.
[04:59] Jordan: maybe schedule a 20-minute follow-up demo on routing policies and canary rollouts — who from Bluewave would attend?
[05:05] Marta: probably Ethan and product ops, maybe one person from data infra.
[05:09] Jordan: great.
[05:11] Priya: small note — the last bench run hit an outlier where p99 spiked to 1.8s during a GC pause on the worker; we're working to mitigate by adjusting model worker pool sizing and max tokens per worker. it's the sort of thing we like to tune during POC.
[05:29] Ethan: ok please include that in the logs, we want to correlate with our infra metrics.
[05:34] Priya: will do.
[05:36] Dana: any compliance paperwork we should expect? SOC2, ISO, data processing addendum?
[05:41] Jordan: yes we'll send the SOC2 attestation snapshot and a sample DPA; the full ISO cert is on our portal but we can provide the relevant extracts for your review.
[05:51] Dana: good. also, do you retain raw prompts by default?
[05:54] Priya: by default hosted retention is 30 days; for POC we can disable retention or set to a short window per your policy. we'll document the exact flags.
[06:03] Jordan: cool. quick timing roundup — action items and owners we've recorded; any other blockers?
[06:10] Ethan: only the VPC peering acceptance and the SAML audience mismatch.
[06:14] Marta: and getting two test accounts for RBAC testing.
[06:18] Jordan: we'll push the SAML checklist and RBAC matrix today; Priya will post raw bench logs by Monday.
[06:24] Priya: yes, and I'll add the KV-cache run variations and config flags we used.
[06:29] Jordan: last thing — pricing sensitivity came up in previous thread; CumulusAI was mentioned as a competitor who sells lower-cost tokens but with higher latencies. any final concerns on that front?
[06:40] Marta: cost is a factor but performance and compliance are higher priority for us right now.
[06:45] Jordan: understood. we'll emphasize cost/perf tradeoffs in the bench deck.
[06:50] Marta: ok thanks all.
[06:52] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the routing demo for next week.

End of transcript. Some minor mis-attributions and filler words preserved.
